source_documents.title: Rational Modulation of Excited‐State Intramolecular Proton Transfer, Aggregation‐Induced Emission, and Intramolecular Motion on Polysubstituted Imidazoles

conditions_studied: solution: hexane, cyclohexane, THF, methanol, DMSO

reference_evidence_units.quote: Compounds 4, 5, and 6 showed both isomers (E*–K*) in methanol and DMSO, indicating that the inclusion of a C-sp3 helps regulate the ESIPT effect, though not as effectively as when combined with a methoxy group on the proton donor, as seen in compounds 7 and 8.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Enol (E*) and keto (K*) emission bands coexist; N-alkyl groups and a methoxy on the phenol tune the ESIPT balance.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Steady-state spectra only; no time-resolved ESIPT kinetics.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This effect is magnified when a methoxy group (compounds 7 and 8) decorates the phenolic ring, pinpointing these compounds as leading candidates for modulating the keto-enol ratio due to their values of ΔE°S1 = 1.5 and 0.1 kcal mol
reference_evidence_units.subject: 7, 8 vs 1-6
reference_evidence_units.statement: The methoxy group destabilises the excited keto form (ΔE°S1 1.5 and 0.1 kcal/mol).

reference_evidence_units.quote: In pure THF (fw = 0%), compound 4 already displays contributions from both enol-keto isomers.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Dual enol/keto emission already in THF.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Compound 5 (H; N-Bu) shows exclusive keto isomer emission in pure THF (fw = 0%) (Figure 8c).
decrease in overall emission, suggests aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) of the keto tautomer (keto-ACQ) (Figure 8b and Figure S20b, Supporting Information).
reference_evidence_units.statement: Adding water lowers the total emission, read as ACQ of the keto form.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No packing or spectroscopic evidence for the quenching interaction.

reference_evidence_units.quote: it was observed that the keto isomer dominates on both compounds (Figure 8c,d)
reference_evidence_units.statement: Keto emission dominates for 7 and 8 in THF.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Compound 8 (OMe; N-Bu), reveals a smooth and continuous migration from the keto form to the enol as water fractions increase until reaching the fw = 80%, where the enol emerged as the exclusive emissive species
reference_evidence_units.statement: Aggregation in water switches 8 from keto to enol-only emission.

reference_evidence_units.quote: For compounds 4 and 5, emission intensity increased substantially as the glycerol fractions increased, while both K* and E* contributions persisted across all mixtures (Figure 9a,b).
reference_evidence_units.statement: Viscosity raises the emission of 4 and 5 without changing the enol/keto balance.

reference_evidence_units.quote: particularly compound 8, which shows a twofold increase in emission intensity at fGly = 70% with a contribution of only one isomer across all the experiments.
This trend is consistent with the restriction of intramolecular motions (RIM) mechanism, in which suppression of nonradiative relaxation pathways enhances fluorescence efficiency.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Viscosity-enhanced emission is read as RIM.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The moving fragment is not identified; no viscosity-dependent lifetimes.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Viscosity raises the emission, which the paper reads as restricted intramolecular motion (the title's 'intramolecular motion'); a supporting explanation next to the ESIPT modulation. The moving fragment is not identified.

reference_mechanisms.label: ESIPT_PT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Exclusive keto emission in THF and dual emission in methanol/DMSO; ESIPT is the main photophysics.

environment_context: aggregation in THF/water lowers the keto emission of 5, which the paper calls keto-ACQ (E05); no intermolecular interaction is identified

contrast_group.varied_factor: methoxy group on the phenol ring (para to the imidazole)
contrast_group.paper_difference: The methoxy group destabilises the excited keto tautomer (TD-DFT) and lets aggregation switch 8 to enol-only emission; 5 keeps keto emission.
